All artefacts

Countries

Share of the national budget mapped to a plan strategy

A share, so it compares across currencies. The remainder is budget no strategy in the plan claims.

Coverage against the gap it leaves

How much of the budget reaches the plan, against how many of the plan's strategies reach no budget. Both are currency-free. Bottom right is a plan the budget funds; top left is a plan and a budget that barely meet.

Strategies by response orientation

What each strategy proposes to DO, read off its own text: inactive states a problem, reactive responds after the fact, proactive acts ahead of it, transformative changes the system that produces it.

Strategies addressing each risk

A count of strategies, not money: how many of each country's strategies name that risk. Shading is within a country, so read down a column, not across a row.

Click any row for the evidence behind it: the interventions consolidated into it, the plan paragraphs cited, and the rationale for every budget programme matched. A flag is a fact we compute, not a score, so hover it for what it means.

the audit view follows the country filter

How the run went

Invariant checks

Each recomputes a stored figure from its own inputs. These ask whether the panel agrees with ITSELF; the Test Plan gates ask whether it agrees with the source documents. Both are needed and neither substitutes.

The money ladder

Per strategy-year: what the document printed, what its programme rows sum to, what was matched to a plan strategy, and the resulting coverage. A wrong figure is visible by inspection.

What the run flagged

Edge review

all reverse pass baskets thin rationale on a large sum reached twice no rationale marked

Every budget programme matched to a plan strategy, biggest first. A pair reached by both passes appears once per rationale, marked twice; the panel still credits it once, which is why the pair count is the lower of the two figures above. Click a row to mark it, or use j and k to step and y, n, ? to judge. Marks are kept in this browser and go nowhere else; export them to hand them on.

What was read

The files each country's figures were built from, with the checksum they had when this page was written. A number here is only as current as the file beside it.

Cross-country comparisons here are shares and counts. Absolute money is shown per country with its own currency and never aggregated.
